greeting: Good morning, Zae. Monday in Tallahassee is mild and dry with a high near 77F, your calendar is just your three supplement check-ins, and the Carnival trip is five days out with the bus leaving Saturday night.

events.title: Morning Supplements (10/10 Plan): L-Tyrosine, L-Theanine, two Omega soft gels, Vitamin D3 + K2, and B-Complex.
Afternoon Supplements (10/10 Plan): L-Tyrosine and one or two Omega soft gels.
Night Supplements (10/10 Plan): L-Theanine and three Neuro-Mag capsules. Creatine 5g any time today.

projectMove.title: Cruise: close the last two open choices this week
projectMove.body: Online check-in is already done and you are in boarding group C02 with an 11:00 to 11:30 AM arrival, so the only open items are your dinner time and your bed setup in the Carnival planner. Settling both before Saturday means nothing is left to decide at the pier, and it gives you the rest of the week for packing and errands.

tip.title: Start a staging pile tonight
tip.body: Pick one corner and drop cruise items there as you think of them this week: passport card, phone charger, medications and supplements in a day box, and one light jacket for the air conditioned ship. By Friday night packing becomes a ten minute job instead of a scramble before the bus.

extras.cruiseNote: The trip runs October 31 to November 5. The Tallahassee bus leaves the night of October 31, the ship sails from Tampa on November 1, and your boarding pass is already saved. Express Debarkation is a separate step on November 4.
extras.weatherNote: Mostly cloudy and dry today with a high near 77F, no rain expected, and a cool low near 59F tonight.

surprise.title: The Hunter's Moon peaked just after midnight
surprise.body: October's full moon, traditionally called the Hunter's Moon, was exactly full at 12:12 AM this morning and is still 99% lit. Right now it is sinking in the west over a clear sky and sets at 8:17 AM, so a quick look out a west-facing window before work catches it. Tonight it rises at 7:06 PM, but clouds look likely through the evening, and tomorrow night clears up again. By the time the ship sails on November 1 it will be a half-lit last quarter moon, rising late that night over open water.
